newsitem.title: USA: AOL cooperating with attorneys general.
newsitem.headline: AOL cooperating with attorneys general.

text.p: America Online Inc said that it met with a group of attorneys general from about 20 states on Thursday in what it described as a "constructive" meeting and said it is cooperating with them to address their concerns about consumer complaints.

"We are cooperating with the attorneys general and we expect to work out everything with them in a mutually agreeable manner," said an America Online spokeswoman. "Our priorities are exactly the same as the attorneys general, to provide the fastest access and the best service possible to our members."

AOL's attorneys participated at an all-day meeting in Chicago with the group of 20 attorneys general. The states have received a barrage of complaints from consumers about the problems they are having signing onto AOL's service, or staying logged on once they have succeeded in getting through.
The spokeswoman said no agreement was reached, nor would she give any specifics on what was discussed, such as the requests of the attorneys, some of whom are seeking customer refunds.
"We are just going to have ongoing conversations with them," she said. "We will continue working with them and keep working to address their concerns."
